charts.title: Share of spa-goers who would be happy to visit a spa once open after the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic in the United Kingdom (UK) in 2020
charts.short: Public opinion on returning to spas after COVID-19 in the UK 2020
charts.description: The health and wellness industry was severely impacted during the coronavirus pandemic as gyms and spas were forced to close to avoid the general public mixing in large groups. Despite the close proximity to others that a spa visit requires, a survey of spa goers in the United Kingdom in 2020 suggested that many were eager to return to their health spas. Some 48 percent stated that they would go back straight away, while 36 percent stated that they would return within a couple of [...]
charts.note: United Kingdom; June 2020; 5,000 spa goers; 18 years and older

charts.title: Impact of the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic on the spa industry in the United Kingdom (UK) in 2020
charts.short: COVID-19 impact on the wellness industry in the UK 2020
charts.description: The coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic had a significant impact on the spa and wellness industry worldwide as many establishments were forced to close to avoid gatherings of people in public areas. During a 2020 survey in the United Kingdom, 67.2 percent of respondents from the spa industry stated that the pandemic had a severe impact on their business.
charts.note: United Kingdom; June 2020

charts.title: Most common hygiene standards implemented by spas as a result of the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic worldwide as of March 2020
charts.short: COVID-19 hygiene standards implemented by spas worldwide 2020
charts.description: The coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic had a significant impact on the spa and wellness industry, as establishments were either forced to close, or to implement strict hygiene standards and regulations for their employees and guests. During a March 2020 survey among spa industry professionals worldwide, 92 percent stated that they made hand sanitizer available for guests, while 20 percent stated that they had enforced an employee travel ban.
charts.note: Worldwide; March 13 to March 23, 2020; 511 spa industry professionals; 18 years and older
charts.source: International Spa Association Share of respondents
categories: Visible employee hygiene standards displayed within the spa
No handshaking policy when greeting guests
Visible reminders/signs promoting hand washing within the spa
Verbal offering for guests to santize their hands before a treatment begins
Verbal confirmation from service provider to guest that hands have been sanitized
Temporary stoppage of facial applications (i.e. neck wraps, eye pillow, etc.)
Intake form asking about recent travel locations
Temporary stoppage of treatments that involve touching of the face

charts.title: Hygiene measures that would reassure gym members during COVID-19 in China as of August 2020
charts.short: Measures to reassure gym members during coronavirus pandemic in China 2020
charts.description: According to a survey by Rakuten Insight among gym members in China in 2020, nearly half of respondents replied that they would consider returning to their gyms during the COVID-19 pandemic if the number of people allowed inside was limited. Around 36 percent of respondents said they would like to return to their gym if mask-wearing became compulsory.
charts.note: China; August 6 to 30, 2020; 631 respondents; 16 years and older; among gym members
categories: Having additional cleaning staff to disinfect and sterilize the equipment after each use
Limiting the number of people training at a given time in the gym
Ensuring that all equipment have a minimum distance of 1.5 m between them
Temperature checks before entering the gym
Make it compulsory to wear masks in the gym
Provide ample hand sanitizers around the gym/in each sector of the gym
Introducing a signing in/out system to keep track of who has been using the gym for easier contact tracing
None of the above - I do not believe that anything can be done to make the gym safe as long as no vaccine has been found

charts.title: Leading hygiene measures that gyms should implement to reassure members to go back to the gym after COVID-19 lockdown restrictions were lifted in Singapore as of August 2020
charts.short: Leading COVID-19 hygiene measures that gyms must have for people in Singapore 2020
charts.description: According to a survey on gym memberships conducted by Rakuten Insight, 54 percent of respondents in Singapore with gym memberships said that they would go back to the gym after COVID-19 restrictions were lifted if their gym limited the number of people training there at a given time. The same survey found that 81 percent of Singaporean respondents with gym memberships would go back to the gym once the lockdown measures were eased.

charts.description: Due to the crisis caused by the COVID-19 pandemic in the spring of 2020, almost all Spanish gyms took the measure of furloughing their employees, with 98.3 percent of the surveyed cases as of the end of May 2020.

charts.title: Main solution options for gyms in the face of the coronavirus crisis in Spain in 2020
charts.short: COVID-19: solutions for gyms in Spain for their clients in 2020
charts.description: Due to the crisis caused by the COVID-19 pandemic in the spring of 2020, companies in the fitness sector in Spain had to adapt to the situation by implementing measures to facilitate training from home. According to a survey conducted to more than 400 CEOs of Spanish fitness centers, in 71.1 percent of the cases training sessions were conducted through social networks.
charts.note: Spain; May 8 to 24, 2020; 402 fitness centers CEOs
charts.source: Federación Nacional de Empresarios de Instalaciones Deportivas; Valgo Percentage of respondents

charts.title: Online service models planned by gyms after the coronavirus crisis in Spain in 2020
charts.short: COVID-19: online service models expected by gyms in Spain in 2020
charts.description: Due to the crisis caused by the COVID-19 pandemic in the spring of 2020, companies in the fitness sector in Spain had to resort to online services in order to continue with their activity. Among the companies surveyed with the intention of continuing to offer online services once the coronavirus crisis is over, 72.8% said they want to include them in the membership fee. On the other hand, only 0.5% declared that the online class service would be free for anyone.
charts.note: Spain; May 8 to 24, 2020; 402 fitness centers CEOs
charts.source: Federación Nacional de Empresarios de Instalaciones Deportivas; Valgo Percentage of respondents
categories: Subscription payment service for my clients

charts.title: Share of people who work out at home worldwide as of January 2022
charts.short: Home exercise share worldwide 2022
charts.description: A January 2022 survey worldwide revealed that a majority of respondents did exercise from the comfort of their own homes. By contrast, just under 44 percent of respondents stated that they did not take part in home workouts.
charts.note: Worldwide; January 15 to 24, 2022; 410 respondents; 18 years and older

charts.title: Share of gym members with access to online fitness courses during COVID-19 in China in 2020
charts.short: Gym members with online fitness courses during COVID-19 in China 2020
charts.description: According to a survey by Rakuten Insight among gym members in China in 2020, around 61 percent of respondents who held gym membership replied that they had access to online classes at their gym during the COVID-19 pandemic. Online fitness gained its popularity swiftly during the lockdown in China at the beginning of 2020.
charts.note: China; August 6 to 30, 2020; 631 respondents; 16 years and older; among gym members

charts.title: Gym members with access to online fitness courses during COVID-19 in South Korea in 2020, by gender
charts.short: Gym members with online fitness courses COVID-19 South Korea 2020, by gender
charts.description: According to a survey by Rakuten Insight on gym membership in South Korea in 2020, around 66 percent of respondents replied that they did not have access to online classes at their gym. Fitness centers were impacted by the social distancing measures implemented during the outbreak of COVID-19 in South Korea.
charts.note: South Korea; August 6 to 30, 2020; 2,213 respondents; 16 years and older

charts.short: Share of gyms that offered online courses during COVID-19 in Singapore 2020
charts.description: According to a survey on gym memberships conducted by Rakuten Insight, 62 percent of respondents in Singapore stated that their gym offered online courses during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. The same survey found that 24 percent of Singaporean respondents stated that they had a gym membership.
charts.note: Singapore; August 6 to 30, 2020; 1,428 respondents; 16 years and older; among respondents who had gym memberships

charts.short: Gym members with online fitness courses during COVID-19 India 2020, by age group
charts.description: According to a survey by Rakuten Insight in August 2020, the majority of respondents with access to online fitness courses by their gyms were between the ages of 25 to 34 years. The participants above the age of 55 had the least accessibility to the courses.
charts.note: India; August 6 to 30, 2020; 10,949 respondents; 16 years and older

charts.title: Change in exercise habits during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic in the United States as of April 2020, by age
charts.short: COVID-19: change in exercise habits in the U.S. April 2020, by age
charts.description: The COVID-19 pandemic that spread across the world at the beginning of 2020 was not only a big threat to public health, but also to the entire sports industry. Many professional and amateur leagues and events were canceled and the public was advised to not spend time in large groups or in public areas. During an April 2020 survey in the United States, 33 percent of respondents aged 65 or over stated that they had been exercising less often than usual as a result of the crisis.
charts.note: United States; April 12-14, 2020; 1,486 respondents; 18 years and older

charts.title: Leading COVID-19 related aspects considered when exercising or doing sports in Japan as of February 2021
charts.short: Leading COVID-19 related aspects considered when doing sports in Japan 2021
charts.description: According to a survey conducted in February 2021 in Japan, 64.5 percent of respondents stated that they were careful not to practice sports in areas where the three "Cs" (closed spaces, crowded places, close-contact settings) coincided.
charts.note: Japan; February 2 to 5, 2021; October 2020 survey n=2,238; February 2021 survey n=2,522; 18-79 years
charts.source: Sasakawa Sports Foundation Share of respondents
categories: Practice sports in areas where the three "Cs" (closed spaces, crowding, close-contact settings), do not coincide
Practice sports while wearing a mask and adhering to the coughing etiquette
Practice sports while being aware of the distance to people
Holding back from doing sports at the slightest feeling of physical unwellness
Mainly practice sports that can be done at home such as yoga or muscle training
Using parks and sports facilities at low traffic times

charts.title: Share of individuals exercising before and after the coronavirus outbreak in Denmark in 2020, by activity
charts.short: Exercising before and after the coronavirus outbreak in Denmark 2020, by activity
charts.description: Exercising and sports habits among Danes have changed in light of the coronavirus outbreak. According to a survey from April 2020, the share of respondents doing fitness activities decreased from 27 percent to 13 percent. More Danes (54 percent), however, found time to go hiking or walking during the coronavirus crisis.
charts.note: Denmark; April 16-23, 2020 ; 1,022 respondents; 18 years and older
categories: Ball games (e.g. soccer, handball, basketball etc.)
Other water sports (e.g. sailing, rowing, kayaking etc.)

charts.title: Share of gym members willing to return as soon as the lockdown due to the coronavirus in Spain ends in 2020
charts.short: COVID-19: gym members willing to return to Spain in 2020
charts.description: In April 2020, just over half of gym members in Spain were ready to return as soon as the lockdown as a consequence of the coronavirus was over. Only 11.9 percent said they wanted to wait until after the summer to return to their sports center. The undecided, on the other hand, represented practically 31 percent.
charts.note: Spain; 2020
categories: I am hesitating to go back
I will come back after summer

charts.title: Share of gym-goers that intended to return to the gym after the coronavirus lockdown in Spain as of May 2020
charts.short: COVID-19: gym members intending to return to Spain in 2020
charts.description: This statistic illustrate the share of gym-goers that intended to return to the gym after the coronavirus lockdown in Spain as of May 2020. The vast majority of gym-goers wanted to return to their fitness centers, with over approximately 85 percent in all cases. However, in a situation where the price for the membership increased by 10 percent, the willingness to go to the gym drops by approximately 60 percent.
charts.note: Spain; 2020; 8,259 members*; * Users of 94 facilities. Read more
charts.source: Management Around Sports; Universidad de Alcalá

charts.title: Attitude towards sport activities before and after the coronavirus (COVID-19) epidemic in Poland in 2020
charts.short: Attitude towards sport activities during the COVID-19 epidemic in Poland in 2020
charts.description: Due to the coronavirus outbreak in Poland in 2020, most of the respondents plan to exercise more when pandemic ends or return to sports activities as soon as the sports facilities are reopened. For those who reduced their physical activity after the epidemic, the main reasons were: closure of sports facilities, outdoor sports restrictions, and isolation.
charts.note: Poland; April 23 to 30, 2020; 1000 respondents; 18 years and older
charts.source: Benefit Systems; Kantar Share of respondents
categories: Want to exercise more after the pandemic
Plan to return to the sport classes as soon as the sports facilities open
Limited exercising due to closing of sport facilities
Limited exercising due to restrictions regarding playing sport outside

charts.title: Share of population who were physically active in Poland during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic as compared to the period before the pandemic in 2020
charts.short: Share of physically active population during COVID-19 in Poland 2020
charts.description: Polish people were most physically active during the period before the coronavirus pandemic, with 65 percent of the population participating in fitness activities in January 2020.

charts.title: Have you been training constantly at home since the gyms closed during the Coronavirus lockdown?
charts.short: COVID-19 impact on sports training in Italy 2020
charts.description: According to a survey on gyms and fitness conducted in Italy in 2020, during COVID-19, when gyms closed, most Italians with a gym or sports club membership continued to train at home. In fact, the percentage of people doing home workouts was around 64 percent. On the other hand, roughly 36 percent of respondents did not use to work out at home.
charts.note: Italy; May 15 to 30, 2020; 687 respondents; people with a gym or sports clubs membership

charts.title: Share of Hungarians participating in online sports trainings before and after the COVID-19 lockdown in 2020
charts.short: Participation in online sports trainings before and during COVID-19 in Hungary 2020
charts.description: The restrictive measures introduced to stop the spread of the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic motivated an increasing number of Hungarians to participate in online sports classes. As of May 2020, five percent of Hungary's adult population took part in online sports trainings during the lockdown.
charts.note: Hungary; May 25-30, 2020; 1,200 respondents; 18-69 years
